text:
alex: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I'm seeing a regression on short requests (chatty flows). p50 ok but p95 up ~10%.
maya: ouch. where is it cropping up — init stage or generation?
alex: looks biased to init-stage (the "init run" that warms KV / does tokenizer steps). gen-stage latency is stable. suspect kernel fallback + kv lock contention when batches are very small.
perf-bot: [alert] regression_detected channel=eng-runtime rule=batching-tail-regressions
sahil: can you paste the profiler snippet you used?
alex: quick copy: ```
# perf top (sample)
kernel_selector::choose_variant +0.38ms
attention_kernel_fallback::execute +1.12ms
kv_cache::acquire_lock +0.78ms
batch_formation::handshake_wait +0.62ms
```
alex: note: this only appears when init_batch_size <= 3 and token_budget_init is low (we were defaulting to 2 tokens earlier).
liz: interesting — could be that the kernel selector now prefers a smaller-kernel path that hits fallback for certain seq len. fallback has lock we didn't notice.
maya: any quick repro? a curl against canary with prompt 16 tokens and no prior cache?
alex: repro script: ```
# repro (local)
curl -X POST http://local:8080/gen -d '{"model":"rwi-small","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16,"mode":"init"}'
# run 1000 queries concurrently with ramp to get p95
```
jamie: i can spin a canary with stage-separated queues (init vs gen) + token_budget_init=6. that'll reduce small-batch kernel choices and give KV more time to warm.
sahil: propose we try two quick experiments: 1) separate queues and enforce min_init_batch=4, token_budget_init=6; 2) keep single queue but bump token_budget_init to 8 and add a tiny KV-prefetch heuristic (prefetch first 32 keys on cold).
liz: metric additions needed: tag traces with stage=init|gen, kernel_variant, batch_size_at_dispatch. otherwise we won't know which change wins.
alex: agree. also add a counter for kv_lock_wait_ms per-request.
jamie: I'll schedule an A/B rollout: canary A=separate-stage-queue, B=bump-budget+prefetch. 5% traffic each for 30m.
maya: add test to ensure kernel_selector doesn't flip to fallback on seq_len <= 32 for small-batch if we have warmed KV. might be a selector bug.
sahil: i'll run microbenchmarks for kernel fallback — measure overhead of fallback path vs primary for batch sizes 1..8 and seq_len 8..64.
perf-bot: [note] experiment flags created: exp.separate_stage_queue=true, exp.token_budget_init=6, exp.kv_prefetch=32
alex: quick checklist before canary:
- add tags (stage,kernel_variant,batch_at_dispatch) : liz
- kv_lock metric : alex
- canary rollout plan : jamie
- microbench: sahil
- small stress repro: maya

liz: I'll push metric PR now. alex: I'll add kv_lock metric. jamie: canary starts in ~45m. sahil: will post microbench results in thread.

jamie: canary running. initial 15m looks promising: p95 for init down 6% on A, flat on B.

alex: good. sahil — any microbench numbers?
sahil: quick results: fallback overhead ~0.9ms extra per-request for batch_size=1, ~0.3ms at batch_size=4. KV lock contention increases tail when concurrent init RPCs > 20.
maya: that aligns — small bursts of short chats create many tiny init requests => kernel select + fallback + KV lock = tail.
liz: metrics show stage=init p95 dropped on separate-stage-queue canary; kernel_variant=fast_no_fallback used more often since we enforced a min batch.
jamie: recommendation: ship stage separation + min_init_batch=4 and token_budget_init=6, plus KV-prefetch 32. roll for 24h and monitor.
alex: sounds good. create RFC/pr with these defaults and note we should still fix kernel selector heuristics (maybe prefer primary kernel even for tiny batches if KV warm). sahil: I'll follow up with a patch to kernel selector.
maya: thanks team — nice quick loop. :thumbsup:
